sentences.text: Centenariosuchus is distinguished from all other caimans by the straight outer margin of the suborbital fenestra on the underside of its skull.
It shares a combination of skull features with basal caimans like Tsoabichi and Eocaiman, as well as derived caimans like Caiman.
Fossil specimens of skull fragments were discovered in the Cucaracha Formation in Panama during 2009 and 2011.
The species was named in 2013 to honor the centennial anniversary of the digging of the Panama Canal.
One phylogenetic analysis places Centenariosuchus in an evolutionary group with large, specialized Miocene caimans such as Purussaurus and Mourasuchus.
Centenariosuchus belongs to the subfamily Caimaninae.
It is classified within the family Alligatoridae.
Centenariosuchus lived between the early and middle Miocene in the Panama Canal Zone.
The time range for Centenariosuchus is estimated from 18.5 to 16.3 million years ago.
